properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 6 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current
Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from midnight tonight to
noon EDT Monday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from Sunday
morning through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 17 at 7:51PM EDT until October 17 at 8:30PM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Bay and Gulf Side from Craig Key to Halfmoon Shoal out to 5
fathoms...
Gulf Waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee 20 to 60 nm out and
beyond 5 fathoms...

* Until 830 PM EDT.

* At 751 PM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located near Gulfside 10
Reef, moving east at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* Locations in the warning include...
Gulfside 10 Reef, Gulfside 8 Reef, and Gulfside 9 Reef.
properties.instruction:
Boaters should seek safe harbor as quickly, and as safely as
possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

properties.areaDesc: Tinian Coastal Waters; Saipan Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Tropical Storm Warning issued October 18 at 9:49AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Tropical storm conditions, including winds of 34 to 63
knots, are expected.

* WHERE...Tinian and Saipan Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Damaging winds will continue into this afternoon, possibly
longer if Champi slows down.

* IMPACTS...Damaging tropical storm force winds will produce
dangerous seas that could damage, capsize or sink vessels, along
with drastically reducing visibilities in heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Super Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to move
quickly away from the Marianas. Champi passed close to the southern
tip of Guam, less than 10 NM, as a strong Category 4 storm. Champi
is expected to strengthen further as it moves through the
Philippine Sea, possibly becoming a Category 5 super typhoon. Seas
are expected to remain hazardous through at least this afternoon,
with significant sea heights as high as 20 feet over western
waters, closest to Champi. Dangerous sea conditions may continue
into Monday.
properties.instruction:
Conditions will remain dangerous for small craft, and hazardous for
any vessels of larger size over the waters of Tinian and Saipan.
Stay in safe harbor until the all clear is given.

NWSheadline: TROPICAL STORM WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT... ...TYPHOON WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT

properties.areaDesc: Guam Coastal Waters; Rota Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 18 at 9:49AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64 knots or more will
continue through this morning for Guam. Tropical Storm conditons
will continue this morning for Rota.

* WHERE...Guam and Rota Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Destructive typhoon force winds are occurring in western
waters of Guam, but will decrease as Champi moves farther west out
of the waters. The eye of Champi is now well outside of the coastal
waters to the west. Damaging winds will continue into this
evening, possibly to midnight.

* IMPACTS...Destructive typhoon force and tropical storm force winds
will produce dangerous to deadly seas that could damage, capsize
or sink vessels, along with drastically reducing visibilities in
heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Super Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to move
quickly away from the Marianas. Champi passed close to the southern
tip of Guam, less than 10 NM, as a strong Category 4 storm. Champi
is expected to strengthen further as it moves through the
Philippine Sea, possibly becoming a Category 5 super typhoon. Seas
are expected to remain hazardous through at least tonight, with
significant sea heights as high as 24 feet over western waters,
closest to Champi. Dangerous sea conditions may continue into
Monday.
properties.instruction:
Conditions will remain catastrophic for small craft, and extremely
dangerous for any vessels of larger size over western waters of Guam
and Rota. Waters will remain hazardous across the remainder of the
waters. Stay in safe harbor until the all clear is given.

NWSheadline: TYPHOON WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT
